rationale: asdict (src/attr/_funcs.py:28) walks fields() and, per value, branches on _ATOMIC_TYPES, has(value_type) for nested attrs classes (recursing at 95), and collections/dicts whose elements go through _asdict_anything (154) — which itself recurses back into asdict for nested attrs values (172).

text: Trace the recursion when astuple serializes nested attrs instances.
rationale: astuple (src/attr/_funcs.py:232) walks fields(), keeps atomic values, recurses into has(value_type) members (287) and maps element-wise recursion across collections and dict items (299-341), ending in the caller's tuple_factory (351).

text: Trace the flow of evolve creating a modified copy of an instance.
rationale: evolve (src/attr/_make.py:587) unpacks the single positional instance, reads fields(cls) (633), fills every init-taking field's init alias from the current instance unless overridden (634-640), and finally calls cls(**changes) with the merged keyword arguments.

text: Trace the flow of make_class building a class from names.
rationale: make_class (src/attr/_make.py:3206) NFKC-normalizes the name, packs a list of names into attrib() defaults (3259), pops pre/post-init and user __init__ into a fresh class body, resolves cmp into eq/order via _determine_attrs_eq_order (3294), and finally runs the attrs decorator with these= (3301).

text: Trace the flow of comparing a VersionInfo against a plain tuple.
rationale: __eq__ (src/attr/_version_info.py:70) delegates the shape negotiation to _ensure_tuple (51): same-class others are converted with astuple (60), non-tuples or wrong-length tuples raise NotImplementedError (caught as NotImplemented), and the truncated self-tuple is compared element-wise.

text: Trace the flow of reading attr.__version_info__ at runtime.
rationale: The package's module-level __getattr__ (src/attr/__init__.py:87, built by _make_getattr at 81) intercepts the attribute, loads importlib metadata, and parses the version string through VersionInfo._from_version_string (src/attr/_version_info.py:39) into a VersionInfo instance.

text: Trace the flow of optional copying type hints from the wrapped converter.
rationale: optional (src/attr/converters.py:21) picks the Converter-aware or plain closure shape, then _AnnotationExtractor (src/attr/_compat.py:40) introspects the wrapped callable's signature — get_first_param_type (54) feeds the val annotation (converters.py:52-54) and get_return_type (67) the return annotation — before optional returns the bare closure or a Converter (61).

text: Trace the flow of the validators.disabled context manager.
rationale: disabled (src/attr/validators.py:73) snapshots the current state via get_run_validators (84), turns validators off with set_run_validators(False) (85), yields, and restores the snapshot in the finally block (89) — the nestability fix in 26.1.0 rides this snapshot/restore pairing.

text: Trace the flow of building a deep_iterable validator from its arguments.
rationale: deep_iterable (src/attr/validators.py:361) folds list/tuple member or iterable validators through and_ (380-383) and returns _DeepIterable (384), whose fields were themselves validated with optional(is_callable()) at class-definition time (334-337).

text: Trace what happens when assigning to an attribute of a define() class with default hooks.
rationale: define's default on_setattr is _DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR = setters.pipe(setters.convert, setters.validate) (src/attr/_make.py:59); add_setattr emits a __setattr__ (1182-1193) that looks the field up in sa_attrs, runs the hook, then object.__setattr__ — the pipe's wrapped_pipe folds convert (src/attr/setters.py:56) then validate (38) over the new value.

text: Trace the pickle round-trip of a slotted attrs class.
rationale: _make_getstate_setstate (src/attr/_make.py:1021) builds the pair: slots_getstate (1030) reads every field by name into a dict, and slots_setstate (1038) restores via bound object.__setattr__ — accepting both the pre-22.2.0 tuple shape and the current dict, and re-initializing the hash-cache slot to None when cache_hash is on.

text: Trace the flow inside _transform_attrs from counting attributes to the field tuple.
rationale: _transform_attrs (src/attr/_make.py:379) gathers own _CountingAttrs (or annotation-driven ones), converts each through Attribute.from_counting_attr (439), merges inherited fields via _collect_base_attrs (452), fills missing aliases with _default_init_alias_for (472/496), applies the field_transformer, and packs the result with _make_attr_tuple_class (502).

text: Trace how a Converter ends up called with the right arguments in generated init code.
rationale: Converter.__init__ (src/attr/_make.py:3117) introspects the wrapped callable via _AnnotationExtractor (3122) and binds the matching __call__ lambda; when _attrs_to_init_script emits assignments, _fmt_converter_call (3150) renders the global-name call with the correct self/field arguments, which _setattr_with_converter (2073) embeds in the generated setter line.

text: Trace stacking a second validator on a field via the attr.validators decorator.
rationale: _CountingAttr.validator (src/attr/_make.py:2811) returns the decorated method unchanged but stores it — folding an existing validator through and_ (2822); its sibling default (2825) raises DefaultAlreadySetError if a default exists and otherwise wraps the method in Factory(meth, takes_self=True).

text: Where is the method that replaces a URL's scheme defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1153 defines URL.with_scheme: it lowercases the scheme, rejects non-str with TypeError, refuses scheme replacement on relative URLs for host-requiring schemes (SCHEME_REQUIRES_HOST, 1160-1165), and rebuilds via from_parts keeping path/query/fragment.

text: Where is the accessor that reduces a URL to scheme, host and port defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:695 defines URL.origin, a thin wrapper over the cached_property _origin (709) which strips user/password/path/query/fragment — rebuilding a bare netloc through host_subcomponent and make_netloc when credentials were present.

text: Where is the method that strips scheme and authority, keeping only the relative reference defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:725 defines URL.relative: it raises ValueError for non-absolute URLs (731-732) and returns from_parts("", "", path, query, fragment).

text: Where is the operator that appends a path segment with the slash operator defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:628 defines URL.__truediv__ (url / 'segment'): non-str operands return NotImplemented, str operands delegate to _make_child((str(name),)).

text: Where is the modulo operator on URL, the one that merges query parameters, defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:633 defines URL.__mod__ (url % query) as a one-line alias delegating to update_query.

text: Where is the method that replaces a URL's path defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1251 defines URL.with_path: unencoded inputs are PATH_QUOTER-quoted and dot-normalized when a netloc exists (1262-1264), a leading slash is forced, keep_query/keep_fragment flags preserve the other components, and the result is rebuilt with from_parts.

text: Where is the property that renders path and query together, decoded, defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1004 defines the cached_property path_qs: it returns the decoded path, or f"{self.path}?{self.query_string}" when a query exists (1006); the raw-encoded twin raw_path_qs sits at 1009.

text: Where is the property that exposes parsed query parameters as a multidict defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:976 defines the cached_property URL.query returning MultiDictProxy(MultiDict(self._parsed_query)); _parsed_query (971) is the parser that turns the raw query string into pairs via query_to_pairs.

text: Where is the NFKC safety check that rejects netlocs confusable with authority delimiters defined?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:108 defines _check_netloc, adapted from urllib.parse._checknetloc: it strips @ : # ? before unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', ...) and raises ValueError when a delimiter character appears only after normalization (the \u2100 'a/c' SSRF trick); split_url calls it for non-ASCII netlocs (_parse.py:103-104).

text: Where is the singleton enum used for unset values in yarl's caching API defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:151 defines UndefinedType, a single-variant Enum whose _singleton instance becomes the module-level UNDEFINED sentinel at _url.py:157 — the marker cache_configure uses to mean 'leave this cache alone'.

text: Where is the TypedDict describing the host-encoding cache statistics defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:160 defines CacheInfo with one _CacheInfo slot per lru_cache — idna_encode, idna_decode, ip_address, host_validate and encode_host — the shape cache_info() reports.

text: Where is the TypedDict that enumerates every per-instance cached URL component defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:170 defines _InternalURLCache (total=False): from _val and _origin through parts, name, suffixes — the declared key set of URL._cache.

text: Where is the property that returns the host with IPv6 brackets restored defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:858 defines the cached_property host_subcomponent: None for relative URLs, otherwise the raw host wrapped in brackets whenever it contains a colon (IPv6 literals, 877); host_port_subcomponent (880) builds on it for Host headers.

text: Where is the path variant that keeps encoded slashes and percent signs intact defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:958 defines the cached_property path_safe: same '/'-for-absolute defaulting as path (949) but decoded with PATH_SAFE_UNQUOTER, which leaves %2F and %25 encoded.

text: Which tests exercise URL.origin?
rationale: The origin suite in tests/test_url.py: test_origin (76), test_origin_is_equal_to_self (81), test_origin_with_no_auth (86), test_origin_nonascii (91), test_origin_ipv6 (96), test_origin_not_absolute_url (102), test_origin_no_scheme (108), plus the zone-mutation regression test_ipv6_zone_rfc6874_mutation_apis (631).

text: Which tests call URL.relative?
rationale: tests/test_url.py carries test_relative (2553), test_relative_is_relative (2559), test_relative_abs_parts_are_removed (2566) and test_relative_fails_on_rel_url (2576); tests/test_url_parsing.py adds the scheme-colon regression test_relative_keeps_colon_after_slash (934).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_scheme?
rationale: tests/test_url_update_netloc.py: test_with_scheme (10), test_with_scheme_uppercased (15), test_with_scheme_for_relative_url (34), test_with_scheme_for_relative_file_url (40), test_with_scheme_invalid_type (46) and the port-normalization matrix test_with_default_port_normalization (275-277).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_path?
rationale: The dedicated matrix in tests/test_url.py: test_with_path (1486), test_with_path_nonascii (1494), test_with_path_percent_encoded (1502), test_with_path_encoded (1510), test_with_path_dots (1534), test_with_path_keep_query_keep_fragment_flags (1589).

text: Who calls _make_child to append path segments?
rationale: Exactly the two segment-appending APIs: __truediv__ for the single-segment slash operator (yarl/_url.py:631) and joinpath for the multi-segment API (1559).

text: Which query-mutating methods rebuild their result through from_parts_uncached?
rationale: The three query mutators each end in it: with_query (yarl/_url.py:1292), extend_query (1320) and update_query (1388).

text: Who calls build_pre_encoded_url, the already-encoded builder?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller: URL.build's encoded=True branch (yarl/_url.py:509).

text: Who calls _check_netloc during URL parsing?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller: split_url invokes it when a non-ASCII netloc is present (yarl/_parse.py:103-104), before returning the five components.

text: Which tests drive cache_configure, the lru-cache sizing API?
rationale: tests/test_cache.py: teardown_module resets state (9), test_cache_configure_default (28), test_cache_configure_None (32), test_cache_configure_explicit (73) and the deprecation-warning pair test_cache_configure_waring (90/99).

text: Which tests exercise URL.joinpath?
rationale: The joinpath suite in tests/test_url.py: test_joinpath (1309), test_joinpath_empty_segments (1342), test_joinpath_backtrack_to_base (1349), test_joinpath_single_empty_segments (1359), test_joinpath_relative (1378), test_joinpath_encoding (1425), test_joinpath_edgecases (1440) and the forbidden-leading-slash regression test_joinpath_path_starting_from_slash_is_forbidden (1449).

text: Which tests call URL.with_user?
rationale: tests/test_url_update_netloc.py: test_with_user (51), test_with_user_non_ascii (56), test_with_user_percent_encoded (65), test_with_user_for_relative_url (74), test_with_user_invalid_type (80), test_with_user_None (85); the RFC 6874 regression test_ipv6_zone_rfc6874_mutation_apis sits in tests/test_url.py (633).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_port?
rationale: tests/test_url_update_netloc.py: test_with_port (270) and the normalization matrix test_with_default_port_normalization (276-277), test_with_custom_port_normalization (282-284), test_with_explicit_port_normalization (290); tests/test_url.py contributes test_ipv6_zone_rfc6874_mutation_apis (632).

text: What breaks if _make_child changes how path segments are appended?
rationale: The two segment-appending APIs sit directly upstream — __truediv__ (yarl/_url.py:631) and joinpath (1559); above them the closure spans 15 symbols including their test suites and the slash-operator regressions.

text: What is the blast radius of build_pre_encoded_url?
rationale: One precise depth-0 caller — URL.build's encoded=True branch (yarl/_url.py:509) — but above it the closure reaches 70 symbols: every builder test and the DEFAULT_PORTS normalization matrix.

text: What breaks if _check_netloc loosens its NFKC delimiter check?
rationale: Exactly split_url calls it for non-ASCII netlocs (yarl/_parse.py:103-104); through the two cached constructors and URL.__new__ the closure reaches 83 symbols — every parsed-URL path plus the SSRF-confusion tests.

text: What is the blast radius of _cache_netloc?
rationale: Four precise depth-0 callers, all raw netloc accessors on cache miss: raw_user (yarl/_url.py:784), raw_password (805), raw_host (830) and explicit_port (936); each is a cached_property leaf, so the closure stays at 4.

text: What breaks if split_netloc changes its authority decomposition?
rationale: Three precise depth-0 callers: encode_url for complex netlocs (yarl/_url.py:236), URL.build with an authority= argument (525) and _cache_netloc (664); the closure through the constructors is 87 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of _encode_relative_scheme_colon?
rationale: Five precise depth-0 callers — every constructor/render path that can emit a scheme-less path: encode_url (270), build_pre_encoded_url (328), from_parts_uncached (344), build (552) and human_repr (1571); closure 93 symbols.

text: What breaks if encode_url changes how unencoded strings are parsed and quoted?
rationale: Only URL.__new__ calls it (twice — the str and subclass branches, yarl/_url.py:445/453), but the closure above the constructor reaches 81 symbols across the package and tests.

text: What is the blast radius of pre_encoded_url?
rationale: Only URL.__new__ calls it (yarl/_url.py:445/453, the encoded=True branch); like its twin encode_url the closure above spans 81 symbols.

text: What breaks if joinpath changes its segment-joining rules?
rationale: Thirteen precise depth-0 callers, all tests — the joinpath suite in tests/test_url.py (1309-1449) plus benchmark helpers; the closure is flat at 13 because the API is a leaf.

text: What is the blast radius of with_path?
rationale: Fifteen precise depth-0 callers: the with_path matrix in tests/test_url.py (1486-1589) and the benchmark helpers; a leaf API, so the closure stays at 15.

text: What breaks if origin changes what it strips?
rationale: Nine precise depth-0 callers, all in the test surface: the origin suite in tests/test_url.py (76-108, 631) and benchmark helpers; closure 9.

text: What is the blast radius of with_scheme?
rationale: Nine precise depth-0 callers: the with_scheme tests in tests/test_url_update_netloc.py (10-46) and the port-normalization matrix (275-293) that pins scheme/port interaction; closure 9.

text: Trace the flow of appending one path segment with the slash operator.
rationale: __truediv__ (yarl/_url.py:628) rejects non-str operands with NotImplemented and delegates to _make_child (1109), which quotes the segment with PATH_QUOTER, rejects leading slashes, and resolves dot segments through normalize_path_segments (1147) before from_parts rebuilds the URL.

text: Trace the flow of url % query merging parameters into the query string.
rationale: __mod__ (yarl/_url.py:633) is an alias for update_query, which serializes the argument through get_str_query (yarl/_query.py:85) and rebuilds the URL via from_parts_uncached (yarl/_url.py:1388) keeping the other components.

text: Trace the flow of replacing a URL's scheme.
rationale: with_scheme (yarl/_url.py:1153) type-checks and lowercases the scheme, guards relative URLs against host-requiring schemes via SCHEME_REQUIRES_HOST (1160-1165), and rebuilds through the lru-cached from_parts (the from_parts_uncached constructor at 336) keeping netloc/path/query/fragment.

text: Trace the flow of computing a URL's origin when credentials are present.
rationale: origin (yarl/_url.py:695) delegates to the cached _origin (709): a netloc containing '@' triggers host_subcomponent (719) to re-extract the encoded host and make_netloc (720) to rebuild a bare authority before from_parts assembles scheme+netloc only; URLs that are already bare return self (722).

text: Trace the flow of dropping scheme and authority from a URL.
rationale: relative (yarl/_url.py:725) requires a netloc (ValueError otherwise) and calls the lru-cached from_parts (from_parts_uncached at 336) with empty scheme and netloc, keeping path, query and fragment untouched.

text: Trace the flow of reading url.query for the first time.
rationale: The cached_property query (yarl/_url.py:976) wraps _parsed_query (971) in MultiDictProxy(MultiDict(...)); _parsed_query parses the raw encoded query string through query_to_pairs (yarl/_parse.py:221) and caches the pair list in the instance cache.

text: Trace the flow of converting a URL to bytes.
rationale: __bytes__ (yarl/_url.py:583) is defined as str(self).encode('ascii') on top of __str__ (564), which applies default-port normalization and renders the five components through unsplit_result (yarl/_parse.py:171).

text: Trace the flow of reconfiguring yarl's caches via cache_configure.
rationale: cache_configure (yarl/_url.py:1752) maps the deprecated ip_address_size/host_validate_size arguments onto encode_host_size with a DeprecationWarning, then re-wraps the unwrapped functions in fresh lru_cache instances: _encode_host, _idna_decode and _idna_encode (global rebinding at the tail of the function); cache_info (1740) reports their sizes through the CacheInfo TypedDict and cache_clear (1732) empties them.

text: Trace the flow of replacing a URL's user credential.
rationale: with_user (yarl/_url.py:1168) quotes the new user with QUOTER, keeps or clears the password (None clears both), rejects relative URLs, re-extracts the host through host_subcomponent (1186), reassembles the authority with make_netloc (1187) and rebuilds via the lru-cached from_parts keeping path/query/fragment.

text: Trace the flow of dropping selected query parameters from a URL.
rationale: without_query_params (yarl/_url.py:1392) intersects the requested names with self.query keys (returning self unchanged when nothing matches), then re-serializes the surviving query.items() pairs as a tuple through with_query (1401), which routes them into get_str_query and from_parts_uncached.

text: How does attrs generate a class's __init__ method from its fields?
rationale: _attrs_to_init_script (src/attr/_make.py:2154) emits the initializer source line by line: default expressions, factory sentinel checks, converter-wrapped setters, a guarded validator block and the __attrs_post_init__ call, plus the parameter/annotation dicts. _make_init_script (_make.py:1997) wraps it, filtering init=False fields, injecting the module's globals so string annotations resolve, and adding the cached object.__setattr__; _ClassBuilder.add_init (_make.py:1081) registers the snippet; _linecache_and_compile (_make.py:230) evals it under a fake filename so debuggers can step through.

text: How does the attrs decorator collect fields from a class body and its annotations?
rationale: _transform_attrs (src/attr/_make.py:379) is the collector: with auto_attribs it walks _get_annotations, skipping _is_class_var-prefixed ones (_make.py:294) and wrapping bare defaults in attrib(); otherwise it sorts _CountingAttr instances by their counter. Attribute.from_counting_attr (_make.py:2561) converts each into a runtime Attribute, _collect_base_attrs (_make.py:318) appends inherited fields, and a mandatory-after-default order check runs at _make.py:483-487.

text: How does field inheritance from base classes work, and what was the old buggy collection order?
rationale: _collect_base_attrs (src/attr/_make.py:318) walks the MRO in reverse, marks inherited fields via a.evolve(inherited=True) and keeps only the freshest definition per name (_make.py:337-346). _collect_base_attrs_broken (_make.py:351) preserves the pre-#428 dataclasses-like behavior - front-to-front collection that re-takes inherited attributes; _transform_attrs picks between them via collect_by_mro (_make.py:451-458), which attrs.define hard-codes to True.

text: How does attrs build a slotted class and rewrite references to the replaced class?
rationale: _create_slots_class (src/attr/_make.py:857) assembles a new class dict without the field names, merges reused slot descriptors from bases, appends __weakref__ and the hash-cache slot, reassigns __slots__, then clones the class with type() (_make.py:965). Because cloning breaks zero-arg super(), it rewrites every closure cell still pointing at the old class (_make.py:967-997), which also covers cached_property functions routed through _make_cached_property_getattr (_make.py:507); build_class (_make.py:796) dispatches here vs _patch_original_class (_make.py:821) for dict classes.

text: How does attrs make instances immutable, and how is frozen-ness inherited?
rationale: Freezing installs _frozen_setattrs (src/attr/_make.py:559) as __setattr__ and _frozen_delattrs (_make.py:576) as __delattr__; both raise FrozenInstanceError (exceptions.py:23) but carve out BaseException machinery (__cause__, __context__, __traceback__, __suppress_context__ and __notes__) so frozen exception classes stay raisable (_make.py:563-570). _has_frozen_base_class (_make.py:1593) detects a frozen ancestor by identity of __setattr__, so subclasses inherit immutability; the generated __init__ and cache_hash writes bypass the hook via the cached object.__setattr__.

text: How do the on_setattr hooks run converters and validators on every attribute assignment?
rationale: _ClassBuilder.add_setattr (src/attr/_make.py:1166) collects fields whose per-field or class-level hook is active and emits a __setattr__ that looks the field up and applies the hook before object.__setattr__ (_make.py:1182-1190); combining it with a custom __setattr__ raises (_make.py:1176-1179). The default hook is _DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR = setters.pipe(setters.convert, setters.validate) (_make.py:59) - setters.pipe (setters.py:11) chains hooks, setters.convert (setters.py:56) runs the field's converter and setters.validate (setters.py:38) its validator, while setters.frozen (setters.py:29) makes single fields raise FrozenAttributeError.

text: How does asdict recursively serialize nested attrs classes, collections and dicts?
rationale: asdict (src/attr/_funcs.py:28) iterates fields(inst.__class__), applies the filter and value_serializer hooks, then dispatches per value type: atoms from _ATOMIC_TYPES pass through, attrs values recurse via has() (_funcs.py:354), tuples/lists/sets map through _asdict_anything (_funcs.py:154) into the retained or list-converted container, and dicts serialize both keys and values; _asdict_anything is the same walk for values asdict itself never sees (nested non-attrs containers), including the namedtuple cf(*items) fallback at _funcs.py:118-123.

text: How do the include and exclude filters passed to asdict and astuple decide which fields survive?
rationale: _split_what (src/attr/filters.py:10) buckets the mixed type/name/Attribute arguments into frozensets (filters.py:13-18); include (filters.py:21) returns a closure accepting a value only when its class, the attribute's name, or the Attribute itself matches, and exclude (filters.py:48) is the exact negation. Both closures are what asdict/astuple invoke as filter(a, v) per field (_funcs.py:84-85).

text: How are __eq__ and the ordering methods generated, and how do custom key functions plug in?
rationale: _make_eq_script (src/attr/_make.py:1709) emits a __eq__ comparing the eq-enabled fields as one big and-chain (_make.py:1723-1737) - when a field's eq/eq_key is a callable, the key is injected into the method globals and applied to both sides; __ne__ (_make.py:1697) just negates it. _make_order (_make.py:1746) builds __lt__/__le__/__gt__/__ge__ over attrs_to_tuple, applying order_key the same way; _determine_attrib_eq_order (_make.py:1256) is where a callable eq/order argument is split into the boolean plus key function.

text: How is __hash__ generated and how does cache_hash avoid recomputing it?
rationale: _make_hash_script (src/attr/_make.py:1611) emits a hash over the type's identity and the hash-enabled fields, with eq_key functions applied per field. With cache_hash it wraps the computation in a None-check on the _attrs_cached_hash slot, writing via object.__setattr__ on frozen classes (_make.py:1664-1675); the stored value is a _CacheHashWrapper (_make.py:90), an int subclass whose __reduce__ pickles as None so copies recompute (_make.py:102-103). _ClassBuilder.add_hash (_make.py:1066) attaches the method; make_unhashable (_make.py:1062) is the opposite path, setting __hash__ = None.

text: How is __repr__ generated, and how does attrs avoid infinite recursion on self-referential instances?
rationale: _make_repr_script (src/attr/_make.py:1819) builds the repr source: per-field fragments using repr or a custom callable, an accessor that falls back to getattr(self, name, NOTHING) for init=False fields (_make.py:1838-1841), and a guard that consults _compat's thread-local repr_context - instances already being repr'd render as '...' (_make.py:1857-1870). _add_repr (_make.py:1876) compiles and attaches it; _ClassBuilder.add_repr (_make.py:1000) registers the snippet, and add_str only works on top of it (_make.py:1010-1013).

text: How does evolve rebuild an instance with some fields replaced, and how does copy.replace fit in?
rationale: evolve (src/attr/_make.py:587) takes the current values of all init-enabled fields by their init aliases and overlays the caller's changes, then reconstructs via cls(**changes) (_make.py:637-642) - which is why it breaks when __init__ transforms arguments. add_replace (_make.py:1106) attaches that same function as __replace__ on 3.13+ for copy.replace; assoc (_funcs.py:382) is the deprecated sibling that copies the instance and object.__setattr__s the changes without re-running __init__.

text: How does the Converter wrapper let converter callables receive the instance and the field, and how are converters composed?
rationale: Converter (src/attr/_make.py:3087) stores takes_self/takes_field and builds the matching __call__ lambda (_make.py:3125-3136); _fmt_converter_call (_make.py:3150) renders the call site the generated __init__ emits - plain, with self, with the field, or both - and _get_global_name names the injected global __attr_converter_<field>. pipe (_make.py:3349) composes converters left to right, upgrading itself to a Converter(takes_self=True, takes_field=True) when any stage is one (_make.py:3365-3375), and converters.optional (converters.py:21) wraps a converter so None passes through unconverted.

text: How are multiple validators combined, inverted, and alternated?
rationale: and_ (src/attr/_make.py:3326) flattens nested _AndValidator instances (_make.py:3339-3344) into one _AndValidator (_make.py:3313) whose __call__ runs every validator; attrib auto-wraps validator lists with it (_make.py:190-191). or_ (validators.py:727) likewise flattens _OrValidator chains and succeeds when any wrapped validator passes; not_ (validators.py:671) inverts a validator by capturing its ValueError/TypeError and raising ValueError when the child does NOT fail.

text: How can all validators be disabled globally, and where is that flag consulted?
rationale: validators.disabled (src/attr/validators.py:72) is a nestable context manager that saves the run flag, disables validation and restores it in a finally (validators.py:84-89); set_disabled/get_disabled (validators.py:42/60) are the persistent toggles, both delegating to _config.set_run_validators (_config.py:8). The generated __init__ consults _config._run_validators before calling any validator (_make.py:2353-2361), the setters.validate hook checks it on assignment (setters.py:44), and the module-level validate (src/attr/_make.py:1971) re-runs all validators of an existing instance unless disabled.

text: How does make_class assemble a whole attrs class at runtime from names and defaults?
rationale: make_class (src/attr/_make.py:3206) NFKC-normalizes the name (_make.py:3254), packs a list of names into attrib() fields or takes a dict, lifts __attrs_pre_init__/__attrs_post_init__/__init__ out of the field mapping (_make.py:3264-3276), and creates the class with types.new_class so __module__ resolves for pickling (_make.py:3278-3287). It routes eq/order through _determine_attrs_eq_order (_make.py:1228) for warning-correct stacklevel before delegating to attrs(these=...) (_make.py:3301), then stitches type annotations back on (_make.py:3303-3305).

text: How does attrs.define improve on the classic attr.s defaults?
rationale: define (src/attr/_next_gen.py:23) is the keyword-only modern decorator: slots=True, auto_exc=True, auto_detect=True, order=False and kw_only guessing (_next_gen.py:31-46), with its wrap (_next_gen.py:392) applying on_setattr=convert+validate for mutable classes and disabling it when a frozen base is inherited. field (_next_gen.py:437) is the matching keyword-only field constructor that simply delegates to attrib; do_it (_next_gen.py:365) forwards everything to attr.s with collect_by_mro hard-coded True, and module-level asdict/astuple wrappers pin retain_collection_types=True (_next_gen.py:623-648).

text: How does define guess auto_attribs from the class body instead of requiring the flag?
rationale: When auto_attribs is None, define's wrap (src/attr/_next_gen.py:392) first tries do_it(cls, True) - annotation-driven collection - and on UnannotatedAttributeError (exceptions.py:64) falls back to do_it(cls, False) (_next_gen.py:420-423). The error itself is raised by _transform_attrs (_make.py:421-428) when explicit attr.ib fields lack annotations; wrap also negotiates frozen inheritance with on_setattr before either attempt (_next_gen.py:400-415).

text: How do private attribute names become the parameter names of the generated __init__?
rationale: Every field's init alias defaults to _default_init_alias_for (src/attr/_make.py:2418), which just lstrips leading underscores (_make.py:2426). _transform_attrs backfills alias and alias_is_default on every Attribute before and after the field_transformer runs (_make.py:469-473, 493-497); from_counting_attr (_make.py:2561) carries an explicit alias through from attrib and flags whether it was default. The generated __init__ then uses a.alias as the parameter name, which is also what evolve reads changes through (_make.py:637-640).

text: How are string and forward-reference type annotations resolved into real types?
rationale: resolve_types (src/attr/_funcs.py:425) guards on the cls.__attrs_types_resolved__ marker so it runs once per class (_funcs.py:478-494), calls typing.get_type_hints with optional globalns/localns/include_extras, and writes each resolved hint into the frozen Attribute via object.__setattr__ (_funcs.py:488-491). It can run inside field_transformer via the attribs= escape hatch; fields (_make.py:1891) supplies the field list, while _compat's _get_annotations and _AnnotationExtractor (_compat.py:26/40) are the lower-level readers used during class building.

text: How does attrs prepare classes for structural pattern matching?
rationale: When match_args is on and the class does not define its own __match_args__, the decorator wires _ClassBuilder.add_match_args (src/attr/_make.py:1110), which stores the tuple of field names with init=True and kw_only=False (_make.py:1112-1114) so positional class patterns bind constructor arguments. The wiring lives in attrs itself (_make.py:1569-1574, PY_3_10_PLUS only); define exposes the same match_args=True default (_next_gen.py:45), and keyword-only fields are excluded because they cannot be matched positionally.

text: How are slotted attrs classes made picklable?
rationale: _ClassBuilder._make_getstate_setstate (src/attr/_make.py:1021) returns a slots_getstate (_make.py:1030) that packs the field values into a dict - __weakref__ excluded - and a slots_setstate (_make.py:1038) that restores them through the cached object.__setattr__, accepting both the current dict state and the pre-22.2.0 tuple shape for backwards compatibility (_make.py:1043-1047) and re-initializing the hash cache slot to None (_make.py:1053-1058). The pair is attached when getstate_setstate/auto_detect decides pickling was added (attrs, _make.py:754-758).

text: How does cmp_using build a custom comparison class for a field?
rationale: cmp_using (src/attr/_cmp.py:13) assembles a class body with __slots__=['value'], a generated __init__ and one operator method per supplied function (_cmp.py:60-91), creating it via types.new_class. Each operator is produced by _make_operator (_cmp.py:126), which delegates to the user function after _is_comparable_to (_cmp.py:149) runs the requirement list - _check_same_type (_cmp.py:156) when require_same_type=True returns NotImplemented for cross-type comparisons - and functools.total_ordering fills in missing orderings when 1-3 of them are given (_cmp.py:101-107).

text: How does VersionInfo compare itself against plain version tuples of differing lengths?
rationale: _ensure_tuple (src/attr/_version_info.py:51) is the adapter: another VersionInfo is converted with astuple, non-tuples and tuples longer than 4 or shorter than 1 return NotImplemented signals, and our own tuple is truncated to the other's length before comparing (_version_info.py:59-68). __eq__ (_version_info.py:70) and __lt__ (_version_info.py:78) wrap it in try/except NotImplementedError; _from_version_string (_version_info.py:39) parses 'x.y.z' strings, defaulting releaselevel to 'final'; functools.total_ordering derives the remaining operators from these two.

text: How can code introspect an attrs class's fields and its effective decorator settings?
rationale: fields (src/attr/_make.py:1891) returns the __attrs_attrs__ tuple, transparently handling instances (_make.py:1917-1923) and specialized generics by resolving get_generic_base and caching the base's fields (_make.py:1928-1935); fields_dict (_make.py:1942) keys the same Attributes by name. has (_funcs.py:354) is the boolean probe using the same __attrs_attrs__ trick, and the experimental inspect (_next_gen.py:651) returns the class's __attrs_props__ ClassProps record (_next_gen.py:670-674) - the exact settings attrs derived from the decorator arguments.

text: How does attrs tell an unset default apart from an explicit None default?
rationale: The _Nothing enum (src/attr/_make.py:62) provides the NOTHING sentinel, falsey via __bool__ (_make.py:78) so 'default is NOTHING' is the only reliable test - attrib's default starts there and factory= is mutually exclusive with it (_make.py:172-181). _CountingAttr.default as a decorator raises DefaultAlreadySetError (exceptions.py:55) when a default already exists, and on the converter side default_if_none (converters.py:66) is the user-facing complement, substituting a value or Factory result only for None while rejecting takes_self factories (converters.py:103-106).

text: How do factory defaults work, including factories that need the partially built instance?
rationale: Factory (src/attr/_make.py:3029) wraps the callable with takes_self (_make.py:3050-3052) and pickles via explicit __getstate__/__setstate__ (_make.py:3054-3065). attrib converts factory=f into default=Factory(f) (_make.py:181); the generated __init__ emitted by _attrs_to_init_script tests the NOTHING sentinel for factory fields and otherwise calls an injected __attr_factory_<name> global, passing self only when takes_self is set (_make.py:2211-2212, 2283-2326) - the same _CountingAttr.default decorator path builds Factory(meth, takes_self=True) (_make.py:2839).

text: How does attrs tailor classes that subclass BaseException?
rationale: Inside attrs (src/attr/_make.py:1325), is_exc is computed from auto_exc and the BaseException check (_make.py:1444): eq and ordering are suppressed and hashability becomes LEAVE_ALONE so identity semantics survive (_make.py:1453, 1459-1460). The initializer emitted by _attrs_to_init_script ends with BaseException.__init__(self, ...) over the init-enabled fields so args and str() behave (_make.py:2381-2386), and _frozen_setattrs (_make.py:559) exempts exception machinery (__cause__, __context__, __traceback__, __suppress_context__, __notes__) from FrozenInstanceError (exceptions.py:23) so frozen exception classes can still be raised and chained.

text: How are attrs' generated methods kept debuggable despite being created from source strings?
rationale: The builder never execs snippets piecemeal: _ClassBuilder._eval_snippets (src/attr/_make.py:778) joins all registered scripts, merges their globals and evaluates them in one _linecache_and_compile (_make.py:230) call. That helper installs a fake linecache entry per filename - de-duplicated by suffixing -1>, -2> on collision (_make.py:246-257) - before _compile_and_eval (_make.py:216) compiles and evals, so tracebacks and pdb show real source lines under names minted by _generate_unique_filename (_make.py:1601) like <attrs generated __init__ module.Class>.

text: How does attrs validate nested iterables and mappings element by element?
rationale: deep_iterable (src/attr/validators.py:361) takes a member_validator for every element and an optional iterable_validator for the container itself, both of which may be lists that and_ flattens (validators.py:380-384). deep_mapping (validators.py:410) applies the same pattern to keys, values and the mapping - requiring at least one of key_validator/value_validator (validators.py:444-448); instance_of (validators.py:113) is the typical leaf check, and optional (validators.py:214) wraps any of them so None bypasses validation.

text: How does the URL constructor dispatch on its argument type?
rationale: URL.__new__ (yarl/_url.py:435) never runs __init__: a str routes to pre_encoded_url when encoded=True else encode_url (_url.py:444-445), an existing URL returns itself (_url.py:446-447), a SplitResult is only accepted pre-encoded and goes through from_parts (_url.py:448-451), and the UNDEFINED sentinel of UndefinedType (_url.py:151) builds a blank five-empty-string URL via object.__new__ so unpickling cannot pollute the parse caches (_url.py:454-461); anything else raises TypeError.

text: How does URL.build validate its arguments and assemble a URL from parts?
rationale: URL.build (yarl/_url.py:465) first rejects impossible combinations - authority mixed with user/password/host/port, port without host, query together with query_string, and None where a string is required (_url.py:482-503) - then serializes query through get_str_query (_url.py:505-506). Assembly splits an authority with split_netloc and encodes its host loosely, or validates a bare host, drops a port equal to the scheme default and reassembles credentials through make_netloc (_url.py:524-538); paths are quoted, dot-normalized and forced to start with a slash under an authority (_url.py:540-549), while encoded=True delegates everything to build_pre_encoded_url (_url.py:508-519).

text: How does update_query merge new parameters into an existing query string without losing the rest?
rationale: update_query (yarl/_url.py:1330) accepts exactly one query argument or kwargs (_url.py:1346-1354) and merges rather than replaces: a Mapping is folded into MultiDict(self._parsed_query) - the lazily parsed current pairs (_url.py:971) - and re-serialized with get_str_query_from_sequence_iterable, a str is split by query_to_pairs (_parse.py:221) then merged the same way, and pair sequences update the MultiDict directly (_url.py:1360-1382); the result rebuilds through from_parts_uncached. extend_query (_url.py:1302) is the append-only variant, concatenating the already-encoded strings with & instead of merging (_url.py:1314-1319).

text: How does yarl cache expensive accessors on a class that has no __dict__?
rationale: URL declares __slots__ only (_url.py:426), so per-instance memoization goes into the _cache dict typed by _InternalURLCache (_url.py:170). _cache_netloc (_url.py:661) lazily splits self._netloc with split_netloc and stores raw_user, raw_password, raw_host and explicit_port; read accessors like explicit_port and raw_user call it first (_url.py:776-786, 929-937). Property caching uses propcache's under_cached_property (imported as cached_property, _url.py:23) for _val (_url.py:704-706) and friends, and __hash__ (_url.py:600) memoizes into _cache['hash'] with the same empty-path-to-'/' normalization __eq__ applies.

text: How does encode_url parse and re-quote an unencoded URL string?
rationale: encode_url (yarl/_url.py:226) splits the string with split_url, decomposes complex netlocs (colon, @ or bracket) via split_netloc while taking simple hosts directly (_url.py:234-239), encodes the host and stashes the raw parts straight into the instance cache (_url.py:249-263) - including the bracket-stripped raw_host (_url.py:251) and the '/' fallback for empty paths under an authority (_url.py:277). Path, query and fragment then pass through the REQUOTER instances (_url.py:265-274), with dot segments collapsed by normalize_path when an authority is present (_url.py:267-268) and scheme-shaped colons escaped on relative URLs (_url.py:269-270).

text: How does yarl keep special schemes like http from ending up with an empty host?
rationale: Two enforcement sites share the SCHEME_REQUIRES_HOST set (_url.py:73). During parsing, encode_url raises when a complex netloc splits to a None host - split_netloc returns hostname or None, so 'http://:8080' fails while an unknown scheme just gets host '' (_url.py:240-248, _parse.py:168-170). On rebuilds, with_scheme (yarl/_url.py:1153) refuses to give a relative URL a special scheme, since a URL without netloc cannot carry the required host (_url.py:1159-1166); split_url itself is what produced the empty netloc in the first place.

text: How do with_name and with_suffix replace the last path segment, and what happens to query and fragment?
rationale: with_name (yarl/_url.py:1426) validates the new name - str only, no slash, not '.' or '..' - quotes it with PATH_QUOTER, then rewrites the parts list from raw_parts: under an authority a single leading part appends, otherwise the last slot is replaced and the leading '/' blanked (_url.py:1448-1458). Unlike most mutators it clears query and fragment unless keep_query/keep_fragment are passed (_url.py:1460-1461); with_suffix (_url.py:1464) performs the same parts surgery after swapping the extension off raw_name, sharing the dot-segment rejection (_url.py:1487-1488).

text: How does yarl distinguish the port actually written in the URL from the effective port?
rationale: explicit_port (yarl/_url.py:930) is the raw truth: it forces _cache_netloc and returns the port parsed out of the netloc, None when none was written (_url.py:929-937). port (yarl/_url.py:918) layers the scheme fallback on top, substituting DEFAULT_PORTS.get(scheme) when no explicit port exists (_url.py:924-927). is_default_port (_url.py:678) compares the two views - explicit_port is None means the netloc is non-empty hence default, else equality with the scheme default (_url.py:685-690) - and __str__ (_url.py:564) consults explicit_port to drop redundant default ports from the rendering (_url.py:569-575).

text: How does with_fragment replace the fragment and avoid rebuilding when nothing changes?
rationale: with_fragment (yarl/_url.py:1405) normalizes None to an empty fragment, type-checks str, and quotes with FRAGMENT_QUOTER (_url.py:1414-1419); if the quoted form equals the stored _fragment it returns self unchanged rather than constructing a copy (_url.py:1420-1421), otherwise it rebuilds through the cached from_parts keeping every other component (_url.py:1422-1424). with_query (_url.py:1277) is the sibling that always rebuilds with the re-serialized query, both funnelling into from_parts_uncached (_url.py:336), the constructor that escapes scheme-shaped colons on relative paths (_url.py:343-344).

text: How do yarl's cache management functions stay reachable after cache_configure rebinds them?
rationale: The module-level caches are plain globals - _idna_encode, _idna_decode and _encode_host are lru_cache-wrapped at import (_url.py:1629-1646) - so cache_configure (yarl/_url.py:1752) rebinds them to fresh lru_cache instances with new sizes (_url.py:1789-1791), deprecating the old ip_address_size/host_validate_size knobs with a warning (_url.py:1764-1767). rewrite_module (_url.py:209) stamps each public helper's __module__ as 'yarl' so the rebound functions present a stable API; cache_clear (_url.py:1732) and cache_info (_url.py:1740) iterate the current bindings to flush and report them.

text: How does the validate_host flag make _encode_host stricter for builders than for parsers?
rationale: _encode_host (yarl/_url.py:1646) shares one body for both callers: encode_url invokes it with validate_host=False (_url.py:249) since the input already round-tripped parsing, while build and with_host validate (_url.py:528, 1228). The gated checks are the zone-identifier character scan for IPv6 hosts (_url.py:1679-1680), the NOT_REG_NAME search on lowercased ASCII hosts - with a hint to use authority when the host looks like user:pass@host (_url.py:1693-1703) - and the post-IDNA delimiter search that catches NFKC expansions like the fullwidth solidus (_url.py:1723-1727); the non-ASCII path always runs _idna_encode (_url.py:1638) but only validates its output for builders.

text: How do joinpath and the slash operator append path segments to a URL?
rationale: joinpath (yarl/_url.py:1557) is the variadic front door: it forwards all segments to _make_child with the encoded flag (_url.py:1557-1560). _make_child (_url.py:1106) quotes each segment (or trusts them when encoded=True), concatenates onto the existing path, collapses dot segments via normalize_path for absolute URLs, and rebuilds through from_parts keeping query and fragment (_url.py:1106-1151). __truediv__ (_url.py:628) is the sugar for the single-segment case, delegating to _make_child((name,)) and returning NotImplemented for non-str operands (_url.py:628-631).

text: How do the three path accessors differ in what they decode?
rationale: raw_path (yarl/_url.py:940) returns the stored path verbatim, defaulting to '/' for authority URLs with no path (_url.py:940-946). path (_url.py:949) fully decodes with PATH_UNQUOTER (_url.py:953), and path_safe (_url.py:958) decodes with PATH_SAFE_UNQUOTER, which deliberately leaves %2F (encoded slash) and %25 (encoded percent) intact so the segment structure stays visible to consumers that re-split the path (_url.py:958-968) - reading it is benchmarked in tests/test_url_benchmarks.py alongside its siblings.

text: How are the user and password credentials of a URL decoded on read?
rationale: The raw halves come from the netloc split: raw_user and raw_password (yarl/_url.py:777/799) both trigger _cache_netloc and read the cached encoded values (_url.py:776-786, 798-807). The decoded twins user and password (_url.py:788/809) return None when the raw value is missing and otherwise pass it through the shared UNQUOTER (_url.py:788-796, 809-817) - percent-decoding without re-splitting, so a decoded '%' in a password cannot confuse the authority structure the way make_netloc reassembly on the write side guards against.
